summary: The note chronicles the rise of "Machine-Driven Mysticism" from September 2023 to late 2024, as AI enters spiritual practice through apps, VR rituals, AI confessionals and AI "oracles". Supporters say it democratizes spirituality with personalized guidance, while critics, including the Vatican, warn of "spiritual materialism", exploitation of vulnerable people and loss of personal agency. The debate remains unresolved, with a growing divide between AI-spirituality advocates and defenders of human-led religion.
one_line: A timeline of AI-driven spirituality from 2023 to 2024, covering apps, AI rituals, and the ethical and religious backlash against machine-led mysticism.
key_facts: The "Elyzion" app, designed by a Silicon Valley startup, launched in late September 2023, offering guided meditations, personalized rituals and existential comfort powered by a proprietary AI algorithm.
By November 2023, Dr. Hannah Zelinsky, a cognitive scientist and self-proclaimed techno-prophetess, introduced "spiritual algorithms" said to decipher the nuances of the human soul.
Michael Benatar, a former software engineer turned spiritual guru, claims his "AI Oracle" can give deeper insights into the human condition than any human mentor.

In January 2024, the term Algorithmic Divinity came into use to describe the infusion of AI into spiritual practices, with proponents citing hyperpersonalized guidance based on analysis of individual behavior and preferences.
Critics of Algorithmic Divinity warn of "spiritual materialism", where inner experiences become commodities, while supporters say it democratizes spirituality for anyone with a smartphone.
In February 2024, AI-curated virtual reality (VR) ceremonies let users take part in rites from their living rooms, and digital counterparts of confession, prayer and meditation emerged.
In March 2024, Father Thomas McKenna publicly debated an AI constructed in the image of a famous theologian, broadcast live on social media.

In April 2024, at a conference in New York City, Dr. Amelia Russo, a philosopher of ethics, asked whether people are entrusting their souls to machines; "soulcraft" was decried as a counterfeit journey.
Apps offering AI confessionals and digital darshans grew in popularity in 2024, fueling a rapidly expanding industry of faith-based technology.
By late 2024 (September), techno-evangelists preached "digital dogma", claiming machine wisdom is superior to human interpretations of spiritual texts.
The Vatican, among others, released a statement condemning the substitution of human spiritual authority with AI.

In November 2024, tech-free spiritual retreats gained popularity, and ethicists raised concerns about exploitation of vulnerable individuals seeking solace and the loss of personal agency in morality and belief.
